# Studienstiftung Summary
The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes was initially founded in Dresden in 1925 as a department of the Deutsche Studentenschaft. It was dissolved under National Socialism in 1934 and subsequently reformed as a registered association in Cologne in 1948.
The organization offers a general scholarship that includes both financial and academic support for bachelor's and master's studies, with eligibility based on criteria similar to BAföG. It accepts exceptionally talented students and doctoral candidates based on principles of "excellence, initiative and responsibility." Admission occurs through several channels, including nomination by schools, by professors, by examination boards, via national competition winners, or through an assessment test, in addition to nomination by alumni. The scholarship provides a monthly allowance and subsidies for insurance, with doctoral scholars receiving a higher monthly award.
